text: Git branching is a powerful feature that helps teams manage their work efficiently. Instead of everyone working on the same codebase at once, developers create separate feature branches for new tasks or experiments. This keeps the main branch stable and usable at all times. Once a feature is complete, it can be merged back into the main branch. However, before merging, most teams use pull requests to review the code. This allows other developers to check for errors, suggest improvements, and discuss changes. This simple version control workflow makes collaboration safer and more organized. By using branches, you can try new ideas without breaking existing code, and you always have a clear record of what was changed and why.
